text:
Maya: Heads-up — nightly eval (suite: nightly_quality) flagged a 2.4% drop in exact-match on the common QA prompt set vs yesterday for model redwood-base-v2-quant. Run id: nightly/2024-11-01. Small sample attached in thread.
Aj: Did the quantization pipeline change? Which recipe was used (per-channel, per-tensor, symmetric)?
Sasha: Pipeline used: quantizer v3.1 (per-channel symmetric, 8-bit calibrate on 5k samples). No other model code changes between builds. I pulled examples — many are truncated or introduce wrong proper nouns.
Maya: Example from eval (truncated to short):
```
Prompt: "Who wrote To Kill a Mockingbird?"
Ref: "Harper Lee"
redwood-base-v2-fp16: "Harper Lee"
redwood-base-v2-quant: "Harper Lee in 2019"
```
Aj: That looks like a generation drift rather than just scoring noise. Could be calibration overflow in attention outputs or altered softmax temperature due to quantized logits.
Eva-ML: I ran a quick diff of logits for the same input between fp16 vs quant on 3 examples — layer 10 activations show high relative error and some values clipped to max-int8 range. Likely per-channel scale mismatch on a subset of heads.
Zane: infra-bot, can you paste the nightly build metadata? I want model binary hash and quant config.
infra-bot: nightly-job 1720754800 completed. artifacts: model/redwood-base-v2-quant/sha256:abc123, quant-config: {"scheme":"per-channel","bits":8,"clip":"mse-calib-5k"}
Sasha: Repro steps I used:
```
python -m eval.run --suite nightly_quality --model redwood-base-v2-quant --seed 42 --limit 200
# compare logits:
python -m tooling.logit_diff --model-a redwood-base-v2-fp16 --model-b redwood-base-v2-quant --prompts prompts/common_qa.json
```
Maya: Good. Can someone run a local forward with mixed precision (fp16) vs quant but with the same RNG/temperature to isolate logits vs sampling differences?
Aj: On it. I suspect an issue introduced during per-channel scale computation: our calibration set drifted — we used 5k random samples last night but the distribution included long-context system messages that skew scales.
Eva-ML: Confirmed: when re-calibrating on the curated 5k-called-for-calib (shorter QA-like contexts), the clip values change and EM drop disappears in a 200-sample subset. So root cause = calibration set mismatch causing per-channel scale over-clipping on some attention heads.
Zane: Mitigation options:
- Immediate rollback to redwood-base-v2-fp16 in hosted for all traffic (costly) OR
- Halt rollout of quant model and route traffic to canary fp16, keep quant disabled in Dedicated pools OR
- Re-run quant with curated calibration set and promote after canary pass.
Maya: Let's avoid full rollback unless needed. Action plan proposed:
1) Freeze the quant rollout (stop auto-promote) — owner: Zane — INF-4231
2) Re-run quant calibration with curated short-context set; produce new artifact redwood-base-v2-quant-cali2 — owner: Sasha — INF-4232
3) Add nightly gating: if exact-match drops >1.0% on seeded common_qa or hallucination count >1% then fail promotion — owner: Eva-ML — INF-4233
4) Canary new quant artifact to 5% traffic for 24 hours with telemetry on EM, perplexity, and hallucination signals — owner: Maya — INF-4234
5) Backfill regression test in PR pipeline using the seed prompts used here — owner: Aj — INF-4235
Sasha: I'll also add a quick diagnostic in the quant pipeline to emit per-layer relative error histograms and calibration sample percentile summaries — should help catch drift earlier.
Aj: Temporary workaround: force model selection policy to prefer fp16 for QA routes by adding a routing rule "qa.* -> fp16" in console until canary passes.
infra-bot: Routing change request created: RQ-9829, pending approval.
Maya: Timeline: Sasha does recalibration now, we'll run nightly_quality smoke locally and if EM recovers we'll push to canary in ~3 hours. If canary passes metrics for 24h, schedule automated promotion with new gating rules.
Eva-ML: Long-term: add a calibration dataset that mirrors each eval suite (qa_calib, conv_calib, summarization_calib) to be used by quant jobs. Also add per-head outlier clipping instead of global clipping.
Zane: I'll open follow-ups for implementation items: INF-4236 (calib datasets), INF-4237 (per-head clipping), INF-4238 (improved quant CI).
Maya: TL;DR root cause: quant calibration set drift produced bad per-channel scales -> clipped activations in middle layers -> generation drift on QA prompts. Immediate mitigations: freeze rollout, recalibrate with curated set, canary 5%, add gating rules and eval-based PR checks. Owners assigned above.
Aj: I'll record a short RCA doc once we have the final diffs and link it to INF-4231.
Maya: Thanks all — please update your INF tickets with progress. I'll message product/support to notify customers on dedicated plans if we extend canary window.
Sasha: Uploading the new quant artifact when ready.
